messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A shelf of half-used labels and tape; then several items no longer have obvious homes. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i put the shelf on the table and keep the label with one loose screw. then i put the tape over the screw, but the shelf stays. i move the shelf back and put the label back beside it. i put the tape back on the shelf, but the shelf stays. i put the label back on the shelf, but i move the shelf so the screw stays."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i put the last label on the shelf. i put the tape in the corner and mark the place with the old label. the tape stays on the shelf. i do not check the others. i leave the label beside the tape and put the tape back on the shelf."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i put one label near the shelf and leave the tape there. i mark the spot with a pencil, then turn it by hand. i wait for the next label to leave, then mark the tape once more. if it still sticks, i leave the label alone and keep the tape."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i tap the label with my thumbnail and find a tiny screw that clicks against the shelf edge. i leave it there and trace the tape with my finger. the labels remain tangled, so i put a folded card over them and count the screws. one catches on a screw in the seam, so i leave the shelf untouched."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I tap each label twice, then leave the tape inside. I tap the shelf again and leave a strip of tape on the shelf edge. I keep the label with the strip, but I tap the shelf with my heel, so the tape slips. I keep the strip, but I put a folded strip of paper beneath it and count each item twice."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "I rub my palm and tap the tape once. \"No,\" I say. I scrape a small mark on the label, then put it back. I turn the shelf a fraction, then look at the label again. \"no.\" I scrape another label, then leave it alone."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i mark the half-used label with a pencil and put the tape back. “the shelf is empty, not a home.” i leave the tape in the corner. “i know i can prove i left something.” i mark the second half with a pen. “i still have one label.” i leave the shelf open. “i’ll write the new home on the old.”"}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I rub my sore palm and take one label from the half-used pile. I tap it once, then mark it with a pencil. I put it back on the shelf, then look at the tape. I mark the label as old and leave the half-used label aside. I keep the half-used label in my pocket, not in the shelf. I leave the tape where it belongs, and I watch the labels change."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "the label clicks. my grip tightens. “i put it down,” i say, then move the tape. “i put it down again.” i watch the label’s edge. “i do not know why it stopped.”"}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I take the label from the tin cup and hold it against the light. \"Old one.\" I put it beside the empty place. \"The other half stays.\" I look at the tape. \"The one I put there was older.\" I put the label back beside it. \"The others may be here now.\""}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I pull the label with the wrench. “That one,” I say. Then I look at the empty shelf. “Maybe I left the wrench there.”"}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i lay the tape along the shelf and mark the corner where the label still slips. i tap the tape once and leave it there for now. then i turn the label once and mark the corner again."}]
